steps.note: App stores '' instead of NULL for guest orders from now on (rolling update, no downtime).
Let the old pods finish their in-flight requests and exit.
Forbid new NULL emails: CHECK constraint NOT VALID (no table scan, momentary lock). Short lock_timeout with retries so app queries never queue behind a waiting ALTER.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders'; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the CHECK constraint: full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL: Postgres uses the validated CHECK to skip the table scan, so the exclusive lock is momentary. Same lock_timeout + retry.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders'; END $$;

DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders'; END $$;
